entities.label: Person
entities.summary: ʻAbd al-Salām ibn Mashīsh al-ʻAlamī (b. ?–1227), a Sufi saint from Córdoba, Spain, played a pivotal role in the Almohad Caliphate. Born in the Iberian Peninsula, he was influenced by the writings of Ibn Arabi and the teachings of the Murabitun. As a spiritual leader, he attracted followers from across the Islamic world. His legacy continued through the establishment of Sufi orders and the spread of Islamic mysticism. He is remembered as a unifying figure for the Almohad people, bringing together disparate factions. His teachings emphasized the importance of love, tolerance, and spiritual growth. As a result, he has been recognized as a key figure in the history of Islamic mysticism, influencing generations of Sufis to come.
